Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

hwatch
======

A modern alternative to the watch command. hwatch records command execution results, keeps a history, and can show diffs between runs.

Features
--------
- Records command outputs over time and keeps a history of results.
- Shows differences between executions and supports multiple diff modes.
- Can output results as JSON logs.
- Customizable keybindings and display options.
- Supports ANSI color codes and scrollable output.

Usage
-----
Run hwatch followed by the command you want to monitor. Example:

    hwatch [OPTIONS] [command]...

Common options (user-facing):
- -b, --batch       : Output execution results to stdout instead of the UI.
- -c, --color       : Interpret ANSI color and style sequences in command output.
- -n, --interval    : Seconds to wait between updates (default: 2).
- -l, --logfile     : Write execution history as a JSON log file.
- -h, --help        : Print help.

Configuration
-------------
You can set default options using an environment variable (for example, HWATCH) if you want to always enable certain flags.

Examples
--------
Run a command every 3 seconds:

    hwatch -n 3 command...

Log command outputs to a JSON file:

    hwatch -n 3 -l hwatch_log.json command...

Additional help
---------------
See the manual pages in the man/ directory (if present) or run `hwatch --help` for a full list of options and keybindings.

% hwatch(1) Version 0.3.16 | A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

NAME
====

**hwatch** - A modern alternative to the watch command, records the differences in execution results and can check this differences at after.

SYNOPSIS
========

| **hwatch** \[*options*] *command*

DESCRIPTION
===========

**hwatch** is like *watch* command, repeatedly executes a *command* and displays its output.
However, the output results can be scrolled and displayed.
In addition, the difference of the execution result is recorded with the time stamp, and it can be checked later.
When checking, it is also possible to display the diff with the previous difference together.

If you specify it with options, the execution result can be recorded as a log with json.


Flags
-----

-h, \--help

:   Prints help information


-V, \--version

:   Prints version information


-b, \--batch

:   Output execution results to stdout. NOTE: Operations with TUI are not possible in batch mode.


-B, \--beep

:   beep if command has a change result.


\--border

:   Surround each pane with a border frame


\--with-scrollbar

:   When the border option is enabled, display scrollbar on the right side of watch pane.


\--mouse

:   enable mouse wheel support. With this option, copying text with your terminal may be harder. Try holding the Shift key.


-c, \--color

:   Interpret ANSI colors and style sequences and display in color. It can be changed later by key binding.


-r, \--reverse

:   Display text upside down.


-C, \--compress

:   Compress data in memory. Note: If the output of the command is small, you may not get the desired effect.


-t, \--no-title

:   Hide the UI on start. Use `t` to toggle it.


\--enable-summary-char

:   collect character-level diff count in summary.


-N, \--line-number

:   Show line number.


\--no-help-banner

:   Hide the "Display help with h key" message


\--no-summary


:   disable the calculation for summary that is running behind the scenes, and disable the summary function in the first place.


-x, \--exec

:   Run the command directly, not through the shell. Much like the `-x` option of the watch command.


-O, \--diff-output-only

:   Display only the lines with differences during `line` diff and `word` diff.

\--precise

:   Attempt to run as close to the interval as possible, regardless of how long the command takes to run.

Options
-------

-A, \--aftercommand *command to execute after difference occurs*

:   Executes the specified command if the output changes. Information about changes is stored in json format in environment variable `${HWATCH_DATA}`.


-l, \--logfile *logfile*

:   Output the command execution result and its time as a log in json. The execution results that are recorded are only those that differ from the previous execution results.
:   If a log file is already used, its contents will be read and executed.


-s, \--shell *shell command*

:   shell to use at runtime. can  also insert the command to the location specified by {COMMAND}.


-n, \--interval *seconds*

:   Specify update interval. The command will not allow quicker than **0.001** second interval, in which the smaller values are converted. Both '.' and ',' work for any locales.


-L, \--limit *limit num*

:   Set the number of history records to keep. only work in watch mode. Set `0` for unlimited recording. (default: 5000) [default: 5000]


\--tab-size *num*

:   Specifying tab display size. default 4 char.


-d, \--differences *[none, watch, line, word]*

:   set diff mode. highlight changes between updates. If only `-d` is specified, it will be a watch diff.

      *plane* ... Do not show diff (default).

      *watch* ... Diff like watch command. Specifying the *-d* option applies this mode.

      *line*  ... Can be done diff in line units.

      *word*  ... Can be done diff in line word units.



-o, \--output *[output, stdout, stderr]*

:   set output mode. If you specify the output mode, the history pane will also display only the history where the specified output mode has changed.


-K, \--keymap *keymap*

:   Customize Keymap.　Keymap is specified in the format of *key=action* or *modifierkey-key=action*


Configuration
-------

If you always want to use some command-line options, you can set them in the
`HWATCH` environment variable. For example, if you use `bash`, you can add
the following to your `.bashrc`:

```bash
export HWATCH="--no-title --color --no-help-banner"
```

========

**hwatch** uses *Keybind* for operations on the command execution screen.
It is the default keymap.


h

:   Show help message. Press the *h* key again to return to the previous screen.


q

:   Exit hwatch.


c

import subprocess, os, sys, shlex, textwrap, time
def run(args, env=None, timeout=3):
    e=dict(os.environ); 
    if env: e.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run(["./executable"]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, env=e)
        return p.stdout, p.stderr, p.returncode
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as ex:
        return (ex.stdout.decode() if ex.stdout else ""), (ex.stderr.decode() if ex.stderr else ""), "timeout"

tests=[

for a,env in tests:

        print(f"{time.time()-start:.3f} chunk {chunk!r}")

    if alive(): print(cap(),end="")
    print("<<<>>>")

    return s
def out(label=""):
    print(f"## {label}")
    print(norm(cap()),end="")
    print("##END")
def oute(label=""):
    print(f"##E {label}")
    print(norm(cap_e()),end="")
    print("##END")
def alive():
    return subprocess.run(["tmux","has-session","-t","hw"],capture_output=True).returncode==0

scen=sys.argv[1]

if scen=="basic":
    start("./executable -n 100 'echo hi'",wait=0.7); out("init"); oute("init-e")
    for k in ["n","c","r","d","d","d","d","0","1","2","3","o","o","o","O","t","t","BSpace","BSpace","b","b"]:
        sk(k,lit=(len(k)==1)); out(f"key {k}")
    kill()
elif scen=="counter":
    open("/tmp/hwtest/count","w").write("0")
    start("./executable -n 1 /tmp/hwtest/counter.sh",wait=2.6); out("counter")
    sk("p",lit=True); out("paused")
    for k in ["Down","Down","Up","Tab","Down","Up","Left","Down","Right"]:
        sk(k); out(k)
    kill()
elif scen=="diffstate":
    open("/tmp/hwtest/state.txt","w").write("the quick brown fox jumps\nsame line\nanother line here\n")
    start("./executable -n 1 'cat /tmp/hwtest/state.txt'",wait=1.3); out("initial")
    open("/tmp/hwtest/state.txt","w").write("the fast brown fox jumps\nsame line\nanother changed line here now\n")
    time.sleep(1.4); out("changed")
    for k in ["1","2","3","0"]:
        sk(k,lit=True); out(f"mode{k}"); oute(f"mode{k}e")
    sk("O",lit=True); out("O in none")
    sk("2",lit=True); sk("O",lit=True); out("line only")
    sk("n",lit=True); out("line numbers diff")
    kill()
elif scen=="help":
    start("./executable -n 100 'echo hi'",wait=0.7)
    sk("h",lit=True); out("help")
    for k in ["Down","PageDown","PageUp","End","Home"]:
        sk(k); out(k)
    sk("q",lit=True); out("q in help")
    sk("Escape"); out("esc popup")
    kill()
elif scen=="filter":
    start("./executable -n 100 'printf \"l1\\nl2 MATCH\\nl3\\nl4\\nl5\\nl6\\nl7\\nl8\\nl9\\nl10\\nl11 MATCH\\nl12\\nl13\\nl14\\nl15\\nl16\\nl17\\nl18\\nl19\\nl20\\nl21 MATCH\\nl22\\nl23\\n\"'",wait=0.7)
    out("init")
    sk("/",lit=True); out("slash")
    typetext("MATCH"); out("typed")
    sk("Enter"); out("entered"); oute("entered e")
    sk("C-n"); out("cn1"); oute("cn1e")
    sk("C-n"); out("cn2")
    sk("C-p"); out("cp1")
    sk("Escape"); out("esc reset")
    sk("*",lit=True); typetext("l[0-9]"); sk("Enter"); out("regex entered"); oute("regex e")
    kill()
elif scen=="scroll":
    start("./executable -n 100 'seq 1 30'",wait=0.7); out("init")
    sk("Tab"); out("tab")
    for k in ["Down","Down","PageDown","PageUp","End","Home"]:
        sk(k); out(k)
    start("./executable -n 100 --border --with-scrollbar 'seq 1 50'",wait=0.7); out("border scrollbar")
    sk("Tab"); sk("End"); out("border end")
    kill()
elif scen=="wrap":
    start("./executable -n 100 /tmp/hwtest/wrap.sh",wait=0.7); out("wrap on")
    sk("w",lit=True); out("wrap off")
    sk("M-Right"); sk("M-Right"); out("alt right x2")
    sk("S-M-Right"); out("shift alt right")
    sk("S-M-Left"); out("shift alt left")
    sk("w",lit=True); out("wrap back")
    kill()
elif scen=="summary":
    entries=[]
    for ts,o in [("2020-01-01 00:00:00.111","alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n"),("2020-01-02 00:00:00.222","alpha\nBETA\ngamma\ndelta\n")]:
        entries.append({"timestamp":ts,"command":"cat /tmp/hwtest/state.txt","status":True,"output":o,"stdout":o,"stderr":""})
    open("/tmp/hwtest/sumcmp.json","w").write("\n".join(json.dumps(e) for e in entries)+"\n")
    open("/tmp/hwtest/state.txt","w").write("alpha\nBETA\ngamma\ndelta\n")
    start("./executable -n 100 -l /tmp/hwtest/sumcmp.json",wait=0.7); out("loaded")
    sk("S",lit=True); out("summary"); oute("summary e")
    sk("Down"); out("down summary")
    sk("S",lit=True); out("summary off")
    kill()
elif scen=="outputs":
    start("./executable -n 100 'printf \"out1\\n\"; printf \"err1\\n\" >&2; exit 3'",wait=0.7); out("combined"); oute("combined e")
    for k in ["F1","F2","F3"]:
        sk(k); out(k)
    kill()
elif scen=="logreplay":
    entries=[]
    for ts,cmd,o,st in [("2020-01-01 00:00:00.111","echo first","first\n",True),("2020-01-02 00:00:00.222","echo second","second\n",False)]:
        entries.append({"timestamp":ts,"command":cmd,"status":st,"output":o,"stdout":o,"stderr":""})
    open("/tmp/hwtest/replaycmp.json","w").write("\n".join(json.dumps(e) for e in entries)+"\n")
    start("./executable -n 100 -l /tmp/hwtest/replaycmp.json",wait=0.7); out("replay logonly"); oute("replay e")
    for k in ["Down","Down","Up"]:
        sk(k); out(k)
    kill()
elif scen=="exit":
    start("./executable -n 100 'echo hi'",wait=0.7)
    for key in ["q","Y","N","q","n","q","Escape","q"]:
        sk(key,lit=True); print("key",key,"alive",alive(),"exitpopup","[exit]" in cap())
    sk("C-c"); print("ctrlc alive",alive(),"exitpopup","[exit]" in cap() if alive() else "-")
    sk("C-c"); print("ctrlc2 alive",alive())
    kill()
elif scen=="intervalpause":
    start("./executable -n 1 'echo hi'",wait=0.7)
    for k in ["+","+","-","-","-","-"]:
        sk(k,lit=True); out(k)
    sk("p",lit=True); out("paused")
    sk("p",lit=True); out("resumed")
    kill()
elif scen=="mouse":
    start("./executable -n 100 --mouse 'seq 1 30'",wait=0.7); out("mouse init")
    def send_bytes(bs):
        subprocess.run(["tmux","send-keys","-t","hw"]+sum([["-H",f"{b:02x}"] for b in bs],[]),capture_output=True); time.sleep(0.35)
    send_bytes(b"\x1b[<65;10;5M"); out("wheel down watch")
    send_bytes(b"\x1b[<64;10;5M"); out("wheel up watch")
    send_bytes(b"\x1b[<0;60;4M"); out("click history")
    kill()
else:
    print("unknown scenario")
PY

  HWROOT=/workspace python3 /tmp/hwtest/scenario.py $s > /tmp/hwtest/out_orig_$s.txt 2>&1

done"}

import subprocess, re, os, sys
def fix(b):
    if b is None: b=b''
    s=re.sub(rb'202\d-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d\d\d', b'<TS>', b)
    s=re.sub(rb"thread '[^']+' \(\d+\)", b"thread <TID>", s)
    return s
def run(exe,args,dur=1.1,env=None,stdin=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.pop("HWATCH",None)
    if env: e.update(env)
    try:
        p=subprocess.run([exe]+args,capture_output=True,timeout=dur,cwd="/tmp/hwtest",env=e,input=stdin)
        return (p.returncode,fix(p.stdout),fix(p.stderr))
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as ex:
        return ("TO",fix(ex.stdout),fix(ex.stderr))
def compare(t, env=None, stdin=None, dur=1.1, reset=None):
    if reset: reset()
    a=run("/workspace/executable",t,env=env,stdin=stdin,dur=dur)
    if reset: reset()
    b=run("/tmp/oursbin/executable",t,env=env,stdin=stdin,dur=dur)
    print(t,env,"SAME" if a==b else "DIFF")
    if a!=b:
        print(" orig",a); print(" ours",b)
